missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Замок' is the masculine nominative subject of 'стоит'. 'Старый' is the agreeing masculine adjective, and 'на холме' is the prepositional location. A clean descriptive sentence.

Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Замок' is the accusative direct object of 'посетили'. Because it is an inanimate masculine noun, the accusative matches the nominative. 'Древний' agrees in the masculine accusative.

Strategic focus: Genitive with fleeting vowel. 'Замка' is the genitive form after 'около'; note the fleeting 'о' drops from the stem. 'Высокие деревья' is the nominative plural subject. A useful spatial pattern.

Strategic focus: Dative with motion. 'Замку' is the dative form after 'к', showing movement toward the castle; the fleeting 'о' is gone. 'Старому' agrees in the masculine dative. A natural approach pattern.

Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'В замке' uses the prepositional form 'замке' after 'в' to express where the rooms are. 'Много' governs the genitive plural 'комнат'. Everyday spatial description.

Strategic focus: Instrumental after a verb. 'Замком' is the instrumental case governed by 'управлял', which takes the instrumental. 'Огромным' agrees in the masculine instrumental. A control-and-management pattern.

Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Замков' is the genitive plural governed by 'много'. 'Красивых' agrees in the genitive plural, and 'в Европе' is the prepositional location. Good for plural practice.

Strategic focus: Prepositional with desire. 'В замке' uses the prepositional form after 'в' to express where one dreams of living. 'Мечтаю жить' chains a verb of desire with an infinitive. A wishful pattern.

Strategic focus: Accusative plural object. 'Замки' is the accusative plural object of 'построили'; inanimate, so it matches the nominative plural. 'Эти' agrees in the plural, and 'давно' sets the time. Historical context.

Strategic focus: Nominative comparison. 'Замок' stays nominative as the subject. 'Этот' points at a specific one, and 'больше соседнего' uses the genitive 'соседнего' in a comparison. Strong for comparative practice.
